established: All six learned checkpoints achieved 0/61 SR, 0 SPL, and 0 SDTW.
Each learned checkpoint achieved 1/61 OSR on the frozen surface.
Two unweighted seeds exactly reproduced always-forward on 61/61 episodes; the third did so on 60/61.
Inverse-frequency weighting produced seven STOP episodes across 183 runs; all seven STOPs occurred outside the 3 m success radius.
The unweighted and weighted treatments reached the success radius on different single episodes despite identical aggregate OSR.
Most weighted episodes still used exactly one action type throughout: 47/61, 42/61, and 55/61 across the three seeds.
Across 1,539 sequential decisions made inside the 3 m success radius, none selected STOP; these are repeated opportunities across only two unique episode identities, not independent samples.
interpretation: The unweighted closed-loop behavior is an always-forward collapse on this frozen protocol.
Inverse-frequency weighting increases action diversity but does not recover goal-conditioned stopping or success.
Weighted diversity is primarily across episodes, not sustained within-episode adaptation.
The closed-loop failure is broader than STOP alone because only one episode per checkpoint ever enters the success radius.
Final navigation error can move without improving SR, SPL, SDTW, or consistently improving nDTW.
